principle: Standardize identity and useful role first. Use scenes to explain work. Expand the cast only when a distinct role needs a distinct identity.

primary_specialists.surface: Memory Studio, context packets, knowledge curation
primary_specialists.why: The inhabited shell turns preservation into a distinctive physical idea; calm posture suits patient guidance.
primary_specialists.avoid: Do not make the terrarium a tiny status icon or add human arms. Do not substitute the larger lookdev tortoise for this exact identity.

primary_specialists.surface: Design studio, creative kits, critique and prototypes
primary_specialists.why: Orchid silhouette, rose ceramic and a purposeful material study connect beauty to a visible task.
primary_specialists.avoid: Keep her optional and quiet in forms. Do not make every botanical worker another top-level mascot.

primary_specialists.surface: Research briefs, source maps, evidence comparison
primary_specialists.why: The fox silhouette and amber optical materials communicate curiosity; an archive gives the action context.
primary_specialists.avoid: Never let cunning imply certainty. Avoid unlabeled generated citations or assigning Sable to a model provider.

primary_specialists.surface: Notes, personal knowledge kits, capture onboarding
primary_specialists.why: The compact cap, paper-fiber body and notebook action make a friendly, memorable capture worker.
primary_specialists.avoid: Keep him distinct from Moss: Morel captures the note; Moss curates accumulated context. Do not make retention authority part of the personality.

founder_editorial_cast.why: The verified model sheet preserves a recognizable human author.
founder_editorial_cast.avoid: Avoid using the founder likeness as a generic institutional worker or treating a new rendition as an approved likeness.

founder_editorial_cast.why: Ivory body and twin camera eyes remain readable and already belong to the established cast.
founder_editorial_cast.avoid: Keep the working name and model-provider assignment separate; never label this as the official Codex mascot.

founder_editorial_cast.why: Copper material, round goggle eyes and one ball antenna give a strong owned silhouette.
founder_editorial_cast.avoid: Do not silently rename Brio/Biro variants or present the character as official Claude artwork.

founder_editorial_cast.surface: Community stories, music/making and informal teaching
founder_editorial_cast.why: Scarlet lobster form creates contrast within the established cast without another humanoid robot.
founder_editorial_cast.avoid: Avoid using Riff as the default enterprise-control identity or equating him with an official vendor mascot.

coordinator_working_direction.surface: Mission routing, handoffs and the consequential owner decision
coordinator_working_direction.working_direction: Porcelain automaton, navy textile, open three-arc brass crown.
coordinator_working_direction.why: The mask, tactile instrument and open hand make a strong institutional coordinator; the folio makes the owner decision explicit.
coordinator_working_direction.avoid: Do not replace the four specialists, humanize her into the unrelated Academy edition, or use her crown as a replacement corporate logo. Working direction only; no new public canon or runtime authority.

visual_standards: One material grammar: tactile porcelain, satin brass/copper, optically convincing glass, timber, paper and restrained living ecology.
Keep identity anchors across editions: Moss shell/face; Luma orchid crown; Sable ears/tail; Morel cap/body; Nilo camera eyes; Brio goggles/antenna; Riff lobster form.
Use daylight for making, overcast garden light for memory/ecology, and controlled evening light for research. Avoid making every scene amber, ornate and crowded.
Keep Instrument Sans for interface text, Instrument Serif for selective editorial accents, IBM Plex Mono for technical labels, and current semantic UI tokens.
Write exact text, numbers, source labels, diagrams and UI in native Figma/HTML. Artwork supplies character and atmosphere.
Use a static, quiet equivalent; a character cannot block a task. Small operator surfaces show compact status and real controls before decorative scenes.
Avoid square-cropping a wide ensemble. Preserve 3:2 scene composition and select an explicitly reviewed portrait for 32/64/160 px uses.
A scene is concept art; rendered workrooms are not editable 3D models. Character appearances do not establish tool access or successful execution.

surface_policy.use: Four specialists in their relevant task; Queen only for coordination; quiet mode is available.
surface_policy.avoid: Full-screen cinematic interruption, fake UI, decorative authority or another new face per control.

surface_policy.use: One shared mission and the campus to show a possible future with a concrete entry point.
surface_policy.avoid: Using a fantasy city or environmental scene as proof of actual impact.

surface_policy.use: Core cast and specialist demonstrations with a visible artifact and clear next action.
surface_policy.avoid: Confusing role names, model providers, runtime agents and character identity.

surface_policy.use: Riff, ensemble scenes, gardens and making narratives with more emotional range.
surface_policy.avoid: Borrowed vendor identity, cross-brand canon leakage and unselected founder renditions.

surface_policy.use: Mini Frank with Nilo, Brio and Riff from the established source sheets.
surface_policy.avoid: Substituting any attractive new face or changing the cast through a generated group scene.

leverage_priorities: Make memory/capture kits legible with Moss/Morel covers, useful editable files and one short illustrated workflow.
Use Luma in design kits and critique templates; demonstrate a before/after decision using real editable UI.
Use Sable in research briefs and evidence playbooks; citations and source ledgers supply the proof.
Use the core cast for founder teaching and workshop/community continuity. Character art supports the offer; it does not replace a useful deliverable.
